title: Plant physiology: proposed topics
text: These units organise the planned plant half. They are outlines rather than complete lessons or a confirmed teaching order.

title: Plant physiology: proposed topics
text:
Plant organisation
Connect cells, walls, tissues, meristems and genomes with growth and function.

title: Plant physiology: proposed topics
text:
Resource acquisition and transport
Explain water balance, roots, xylem, transpiration, stomata, minerals and membrane transport.

title: Plant physiology: proposed topics
text:
Carbon and metabolism
Connect photosynthesis, environmental conditions, carbon allocation, respiration and nutrient assimilation to growth.

title: Plant physiology: proposed topics
text:
Regulation and development
Follow signals and hormones through germination, vegetative growth, flowering, reproduction, senescence and cell death.

title: Plant physiology: proposed topics
text:
Environment and applications
Explain stress, biotic interactions, natural products and growth–defence relationships. Connect model systems, transformation, tissue culture and gene expression to plant biotechnology and its ethical questions.
Experiments, literature discussion and scientific communication accompany these topics. Actual protocols and experiment durations remain to be confirmed.

title: Scope and learning goals
text:
Learning goals

Explain animal structure, function, regulation and environmental adaptation.
Recognise representative normal tissues and relate their features to function.
Explain plant organisation, metabolism, growth, development and regulation.
Discuss applications, benefits, risks and ethics of genetically modified plants.
Perform and interpret experiments and write scientific laboratory reports.
Evaluate relevant literature and communicate orally and in writing.

title: Scope and learning goals
text:
How the course works
Lectures and discussion connect mechanisms to observations. Anatomy, histology and physiological experiments develop practical understanding. Reports, literature work and presentations develop scientific communication.
The predecessor assesses theory through written examinations and practical and communication skills through reports and oral presentation. The actual course schedule, compulsory elements and assessment rules will be supplied once verified. See reading and sources.

title: Animal and Plant Physiology
text:
Course material under development



This is a planning scaffold. Topic order and readings are provisional; complete lessons, laboratory instructions and assessment details will follow.


How do animals and plants maintain function, obtain resources, regulate their activities and respond to their environments? This course connects cells and tissues to whole organisms, using comparisons, practical observations, experiments and scientific literature.
The working scope retains an equal animal and plant balance across 15 ECTS. It follows the documented predecessor course while the successor’s formal details are checked.

Practical work develops physiological understanding and scientific reporting. There is currently no required R component in this proposal.

title: Animal physiology: proposed topics
text: These units organise the planned animal half. They are outlines rather than complete lessons or a confirmed teaching order.

title: Animal physiology: proposed topics
text:
Organisation and diversity
Connect cells, tissues, organs and systems. Compare how different animals solve physiological problems and distinguish regulation, acclimation and adaptation.

title: Animal physiology: proposed topics
text:
Nutrition, energy and temperature
Relate feeding, digestion, fuel use and energy demand to thermal strategies and environmental conditions.

title: Animal physiology: proposed topics
text:
Exchange and circulation
Explain how gas exchange, ventilation, gas transport and circulation meet whole-organism needs. Compare animals living in water and air.

title: Animal physiology: proposed topics
text:
Water, ions and excretion
Explain osmotic challenges, transport, nitrogen disposal and kidney function in different environments.

title: Animal physiology: proposed topics
text:
Integration, movement and reproduction
Connect neural, sensory, muscle and endocrine function. Use feedback and reproductive regulation to bring systems together.
Anatomy and normal histology accompany these topics. The exact specimens and practical procedures will follow the established course material.

title: Practical work and communication
text: This page describes the proposed scope. It is not a laboratory protocol or an instruction to begin an experiment.

title: Practical work and communication
text:
Anatomy and histology
Observe representative normal tissues and organs, recognise characteristic features and explain how structure supports function. Retain comparisons between animal groups and the established specimen sessions.

title: Practical work and communication
text:
Physiological experiments
Carry out the course’s established animal and plant experiments. Identify the question, experimental unit, controls, measurements and units before interpreting results. Preserve observations and distinguish variation among organisms from repeated measurements of one organism.
The practical manual, equipment, specimen list and timetable will determine the experiments. No new experiment is specified by this outline.

title: Practical work and communication
text:
Scientific reporting
A report should connect the physiological question, methods, results and interpretation. Explain figures, uncertainty and limitations rather than presenting numbers alone. Software requirements will follow the actual practical instructions; this proposal requires no R component.

title: Practical work and communication
text:
Literature and presentation
Read scientific evidence critically, discuss physiological mechanisms and communicate a reasoned interpretation orally and in writing. Plant biotechnology discussion includes potential benefits, risks and ethics.
